entries.title: Long PDFs count by their length
entries.body: A PDF you add counts against your allowance by its length, one article for every 50 pages or part of them, because a long document costs far more to work on: a 120-page PDF counts as three. Pages are counted before work starts; a longer PDF tells you how many it uses, and one your allowance cannot cover stops with a message. Articles already added keep their old count, and High-powered AI counts an article again at the same number, half that while it is shared publicly.

entries.title: The chat guide can get a mode ready
entries.body: Among the buttons under its answers, the chat guide can offer one that starts preparing a mode in the background without opening it: a summary, the Glossary, Quotes, Ideas, Skim or a quiz. When it is confident you want it and you typed your message, it may press that button itself, at most once per conversation. Chat, Learn and the guide are also told roughly how much of the article you have read, though not which parts, and are asked not to assume you know its field.

entries.title: Larger text and tap areas on touchscreens
entries.body: On a touchscreen, whether phone, iPad or laptop, small text is at least 13px and most buttons and links have a tap area at least 40px. In chat, each web source's 'Bring into this chat' button sits beneath its title, with a line between sources, so it is clear which source it belongs to. With only a mouse, nothing changes.

entries.title: AI-written text has a new typeface
entries.body: Everything the AI writes, from chat answers to summaries, Skim's cues and the notes in the margin, appears in iA Writer Quattro instead of a typewriter-style face where every letter is the same width, so it reads as prose. Code in an AI answer keeps a same-width face, iA Writer Mono, so its columns still line up.

entries.title: Private-link opens are recorded, for the administrator only
entries.body: Opening an article through its private link is recorded: for a signed-in reader, the account, how many times and the first and last time; for a signed-out one, a rough count and the first and last time. Only Spideryarn's administrator can see this, or who owns the article; owners get no list of visitors. The privacy page says so.

entries.title: Backspace takes you back after a jump
entries.body: After a jump to a glossary term, a cross-reference or a section, Backspace takes you back to where you were reading, with your open modes left as they were. It is ignored while you are typing or a dialog is open. Separately, some articles' own markup could switch off the G and / shortcuts; it no longer does.

entries.title: Dictate into four more text boxes
entries.body: The microphone button appears in Skim's box for what you are reading for, Referee's box for a new criterion, the search box in Candidates, which suggests possible reviewers, and a comment's personal note. Buttons that send what you wrote wait until dictation has finished, so a rough first guess is never sent, and a dictated note saves the final words.

entries.title: Going back to Investigate shows your chat
entries.body: In Sources, a chat started from Investigate was listed under Chat, but coming back to Investigate showed what looked like an empty page; nothing had been lost. Investigate now reopens your newest such chat beside it, once per visit, unless a chat, note or comment is already open, and 'Your questions' sits above 'Suggested'.
